The original dataset contains 3, 841 accounts, but we use a lower number of accounts and tweets after ﬁltering them. We focus on accounts that use English as main language.

evidence.title: TexTrolls: Identifying Russian Trolls on Twitter from a Textual Perspective
evidence.text: Therefore, in this paper, we propose a text-based approach to detect the online trolls such as those that were discovered during the US 2016 presidential elections. Our approach is mainly based on textual features which uti- lize thematic information, and proﬁling features to identify the accounts from their way of writing tweets. We deduced the thematic information in a unsupervised way and we show that coupling them with the textual features enhanced the performance of the proposed model.

evidence.title: TexTrolls: Identifying Russian Trolls on Twitter from a Textual Perspective
evidence.text: Thus, we propose the following features to identify these users using only their tweets text: – Native Language Identiﬁcation (NLI): This feature was inspired by earlier works on identifying native language of essays writers [22]. We aim to detect IRA trolls by identifying their way of writing English tweets. As shown in [31], English tweets generated by non-English speakers have a diﬀerent syntactic pattern .

evidence.text: With this representation we aim at capturing the ”Flip-Flop” behavior of IRA trolls among the themes (see Section 5.4). 4.2 Proﬁling IRA Accounts As Twitter declared, although the IRA campaign was originated in Russia, it has been found that IRA trolls concealed their identity by tweeting in English. Furthermore, for any possibility of unmasking their identity, the majority of IRA trolls changed their location to other countries and the language of the Twitter interface they use.

evidence.title: TexTrolls: Identifying Russian Trolls on Twitter from a Textual Perspective
evidence.text: In fact, our goal is to detect Russian accounts that mimic a regular US user. Then, we remove from these accounts non-English tweets, and maintain only tweets that were tweeted originally by them.
